name: Question 17
worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region $D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{{x}^{2}}{y}\,dA & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\frac{{x}^{2}}{y}\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\frac{{x}^{2}}{y}\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}{x}^{2}\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{y}(\frac{1}{3}{y}^{6}-0)dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{3}{y}^{5}\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{3}{y}^{5}\,dy & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{5}\,dy \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{1}{6}{y}^{6}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{32}{3}-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{21}{2} \\  & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The integral is defined over a type II region D={(x,y):1≤y≤2,0≤x≤y2}.

So, we can express the integral as follows:

∬Dx2ydA=∫12∫0y2x2ydxdy

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to x, treating y as a constant:

∫12∫0y2x2ydxdy=∫121y[∫0y2x2dx]dy=∫121y[13x3]0y2dy=∫121y(13y6−0)dy=∫1213y5dy

Then, we integrate with respect to y:

∫1213y5dy=13∫12y5dy=13[16y6]12=13(323−16)=13⋅212=72
